tier_reason: The wiki page is first-party prose with headline ratios against MKL FP32 (via a cited paper), caffe2/perfkernels and FBGEMM's own earlier code; hardware is named for only two results, and no compiler, flags or benchmark code path is given. The cited Marian WNGT 2019 workshop paper (peer-reviewed) could not be opened (aclanthology.org blocked), so B cannot be confirmed.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Wiki page (last edited 2020-01-18): a cited Microsoft/Marian NMT paper reports FBGEMM INT8 at 2x the throughput of MKL FP32 at batch size 1 and 1.3x at batch size 32; EmbeddingSpMDM gives ~2x over caffe2/perfkernels (and 18-25% average-latency gains on production recommendation models); the new 64-bit GEMM reaches 10.5 GOps/s vs 3 GOps/s for the existing implementation (3.5x) on a Xeon Gold 6138 with turbo off; 3D groupwise convolution is 60x faster than the base fused im2col implementation; stride-2 convolutions are 4-10x faster than the existing implementation; 2x-4x speedups at 90% sparsity with specialized sparse kernels.
corrections.caveats: Most speedups compare reduced precision against FP32 or compare against FBGEMM's own older code paths (the 60x and 3.5x figures), so they say little about external incumbents; accuracy trade-offs apply. The MKL comparison comes from a third-party paper ("From Research to Production and Back: Ludicrously Fast Neural Machine Translation", WNGT at EMNLP 2019) that the wiki cites; its PDF could not be opened here. The wiki dates from January 2020, so the numbers are 2019-era. Many wiki claims state no hardware or flags. The MLSys 2021 paper (arXiv 2101.05615) could not be opened (arxiv.org blocked) and may carry stronger evidence. Baselines are not oneDNN, cuDNN or XNNPACK.

notes: All record numbers appear on the wiki page. Metadata from github.com: LICENSE is the 3-clause BSD text (BSD-3-Clause), 1.6k stars, 791 forks, not archived, last commit 2026-10-01. A re-tier to B would need someone to open the Marian WNGT 2019 paper (ACL Anthology D19-5632) and confirm the FBGEMM vs MKL table.

tier_reason: First-party doc that sets FlashRT's own latencies against baseline numbers published by NVIDIA (Isaac GR00T, Jetson AI Lab) and OpenPI rather than re-measured in one harness; a reproduction script exists for the N1.7 Thor rows (benchmarks/groot_n17_thor_latency.py), but no compiler version or flags are stated for the measured builds.

corrections.claimed_speedup: docs/benchmark_comparison.md: GR00T N1.6 on Jetson AGX Thor (T=50): 45 ms vs TensorRT 92 ms (2.04x), torch.compile 105 ms (2.33x), PyTorch eager 117 ms (2.60x); RTX 5090 (T=50, 2-view): 13.08 ms vs TensorRT 31 ms (2.37x), torch.compile 37 ms (2.83x), eager 58 ms (4.43x). Pi0.5 NVFP4 3-view on Thor: 51.51 ms vs OpenPI reference 714 ms (13.9x). On the matched GR00T N1.7 LIBERO harness on Thor (NVIDIA's published protocol, re-run by FlashRT): FlashRT FP8 36.8 ms vs TensorRT optimized + FP8 ~44 ms, and FlashRT NVFP4 23.7 ms vs TensorRT mixed NVFP4 ~40 ms (about 1.2x and 1.7x, derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: README build requirements: CUDA 12.4+ (Thor/Hopper) or 12.8+ (Blackwell), CUDA 13 recommended, GCC/G++ 11+ (C++17), CMake 3.24+ with -DGPU_ARCH (110 Thor, 120 RTX 5090, 89 RTX 4090); the toolkit version and flags used for the published rows are not stated. Thor N1.7 rows were run under JetPack 7.2, MAXN.
corrections.caveats: The doc itself says to compare only rows with matching model, hardware, view count, step count and harness. The N1.6 and Pi0.5 baseline rows are third-party published numbers (NVIDIA GR00T docs, Jetson AI Lab, OpenPI) and were not re-measured; the NVIDIA N1.6 table is for 4 denoising steps while the FlashRT rows are labelled T=50, and their precision is not stated on the row, so the 2.0-2.6x figures may mix precisions and settings. The closest like-for-like rows (GR00T N1.7 on Thor at matched FP8 or NVFP4 precision) show smaller gains of about 1.2x and 1.7x over TensorRT (derived from page data). FP8/NVFP4 FlashRT against BF16 eager or the OpenPI reference adds a precision gap. Repository is new (2026) and all numbers are first-party; the NVIDIA GR00T optimization page could not be opened here (host blocked).

notes: All record numbers appear in docs/benchmark_comparison.md. Metadata from github.com: Apache-2.0, 607 stars, 85 forks, not a fork or archived, last commit 2026-09-30; languages about 45% C++, 40% Python, 12% CUDA. The 13.9x Pi0.5 figure is against an unoptimized upstream reference rather than TensorRT.

tier_reason: First-party llama-bench comparisons with named CPUs and builds; the Jan 2025 wiki page gives the exact script and commits (ik_llama.cpp 3c5f8722, llama.cpp 9f7add1c) and runs the same quantized model in both, but no compiler or flags are stated, so not A. The claim is downgraded because the record's Discussion 8 ratios compare different quantization types, not the same model.

corrections.workload: llama-bench pp512 (512-token prompt processing, CPU only, no BLAS, no Flash Attention) on LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, with the same llama.cpp-quantized GGUF run in both engines (ik_llama.cpp with run-time repacking -rtr) across 17 types (F16, BF16, Q8_0, Q4_0, Q5_0, Q2_K-Q6_K, IQ2_XXS-IQ4_NL) on Zen4 (Ryzen 7950X), AVX2 (Ryzen 5975WX) and ARM NEON (M2-Max).
corrections.claimed_speedup: Jan 2025 wiki page, same quantized model in both engines, pp512 tokens/s llama.cpp vs ik_llama.cpp: Zen4 (Ryzen 7950X) from 1.783x (Q4_0, 146.20 vs 260.71) to 5.179x (IQ3_S, 28.96 vs 149.98), geometric mean 2.883x; AVX2 (Ryzen 5975WX) from 1.524x (Q8_0) to 5.125x (IQ3_S, 44.88 vs 230.03); ARM NEON (M2-Max) from 1.085x (Q4_0, 114.44 vs 124.13) to 7.025x (IQ3_S, 11.34 vs 79.66), geometric mean 3.350x. Discussion 8 (Aug 2024) also gives same-quant rows (llama.cpp vs the fork's own i-quants, ratios derived from page data): 8B IQ3_S AVX2 pp512 28.04 vs 96.28 (3.43x), tg128 6.80 vs 7.62 (1.12x); 8B IQ2_XS AVX2 pp512 46.45 vs 125.46 (2.70x), tg128 10.88 vs 12.07 (1.11x); 7B IQ3_S NEON pp512 12.08 vs 49.72 (4.12x), tg128 10.32 vs 11.11 (1.08x).
corrections.caveats: The record's original figures (6.45x, 4.61x, 4.19x and so on) come from Discussion 8, where the 'iqk' column is ik_llama.cpp's new IQ2_K/IQ3_K quantization types set against llama.cpp's IQ2_XS/IQ3_S at similar bpw and accuracy, so those ratios mix a format change with kernel speed. The 'this repo' column is the fork running the same IQ2_XS/IQ3_S quants, which is the same-format comparison. The Jan 2025 wiki covers prompt processing only (token-generation gains in Discussion 8 are about 1.1x for same-format quants), and mainline llama.cpp has changed since build 4517, so today's ratios may differ. ik_llama.cpp uses run-time repacking (-rtr) for these runs. Compiler and flags are not stated. The README itself gives no numbers. Fork upstream was originally github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp, now ggml-org/llama.cpp.

notes: The record's numbers do appear in Discussion 8, but they are labelled as kernel speedups on the same IQ2_XS/IQ3_S models when the iqk column is really a different quant type (the discussion says so before the table). benchmark_url is switched to the README-linked Jan 2025 wiki comparison, which runs the same GGUF in both engines.
